sources.note: Bibliographic only: zero grammar/sketch/phonology references; 'Data appears in Charpentier, Jean-Michel 1982'.

sources.citation: Aznar, Jocelyn. Corpus nisvai, Ortolang deposit sldr000783 v2 (34 ELAN files, wav recordings, thesis zip) -- file index crawled.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No grammar, phonology or sketch document in the deposit; annotations and audio only.

sources.citation: Aznar, Jocelyn. 2011-2015 Nisvai recordings (Ortolang sldr000783 v2; DoReCo nisv1234 with phone-level TextGrids, doi:10.34847/nkl.2801565f) and Vanuatu Voices audio for 'Nisvai: Blacksands' / 'Nisvai: Ronevie'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No prose description exists; these time-aligned phone-level corpora and wordlist audio are the material from which a stress analysis could be made (instrumental check), superseding the absence of a statement.

sources.citation: Aznar, Jocelyn. 2024. Nisvai DoReCo dataset. In Seifart, Paschen & Stave (eds), Language Documentation Reference Corpus (DoReCo) 2.0. doi:10.34847/nkl.2801565f (dataset-info, README, transcription-conventions files from Nakala; DoReCo language page).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; a 22-letter orthography-to-phone conversion table and licensing text; no stress information.

sources.citation: Rangelov, Tihomir, Mary Walworth & Julie Barbour. 2023. A multifaceted approach to understanding unexpected sound change: The bilabial trills of Vanuatu's Malekula Island. Diachronica 40(3): 384-432. doi:10.1075/dia.21051.ran. Appendix Tables A.2 (p. 420) and A.3 (p. 421).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Table A.2: Nisvai (nisv1234) = 2 Vanuatu Voices doculects, 'Data from other sources for this language? No'; Table A.3 lists Nisvai under 'Languages without phonological analysis'; text calls Avok, Navwien and Nisvai 'under-described'.

sources.citation: Aznar, Jocelyn & Núria Gala. 2020. The Nisvai Corpus of Oral Narrative Practices from Malekula (Vanuatu) and its Associated Language Resources. Proceedings of LREC 2020, 2622-2629 (2020.lrec-1.323).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3: 'Charpentier (1984) described the phonological systems of 19 languages of the South Malekula as a base to undertake his lexical survey'; transcription 'based on the phonological analysis of the Nisvai language.. produced during the fieldwork'; segmentation into Chafe intonation units. No stress/accent.

sources.citation: Rangelov, Tihomir. 2020. A grammar of the Ahamb language (Vanuatu). PhD thesis, University of Waikato. pp. 6-7, 78; Rangelov, Bratrud & Barbour 2019 LDD 16; Lynch 2014 Open Linguistics 1; King, Rangelov & Walworth 2025 JoLE; Schaefer 2023.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing about Nisvai stress; Rangelov 2020:78 'Ahamb's closest relative for which an analysis of stress patterns exists is Uluveu (Healey 2013)' -- i.e. none for Nisvai. Nisvai appears elsewhere only in sociolinguistic notes (Farun, Blaksand, mutual intelligibility), subgroup maps and cognate tables.

sources.citation: Aznar, Jocelyn. 2019. Narrer une nabol : la production des textes nisvais en fonction de l'âge et de la situation d'énonciation (Malekula, Vanuatu). Thèse de doctorat, EHESS (CREDO), dir. L. Dousset & N. Gala. 3 vols (vol. 1 329 pp; vol. 2 lexique nisvai-français; vol. 3 recueil de nabol). NNT 2019EHES0180; HAL tel-02513026.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnolinguistic study of narrative practice; no phonology chapter; 0 hits for accent/tonique/accentuation/stress/pénultième in 329 pp. p. 48: Charpentier's atlas is the 'première description phonologique et lexicographique' of Nisvai. p. 193 fn 196: 'L'analyse de la prosodie ne rentre pas dans notre champ d'étude.' p. 329 appendix 'L'alphabet du nisvai et comparaison avec le travail de Charpentier' = segmental inventories (phonetic/phonological/alphabet rows) only, no stress marks or row.

sources.citation: Aznar, Jocelyn. 2019. Visualisation en arbres pour assister l'étude des sons du nisvai. Poster (HAL hal-02507007).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only other item by the sole modern fieldworker that is about Nisvai sounds; may include an inventory/phonotactic note; behind the HAL Anubis wall today.

sources.citation: Shimelman, Aviva et al. 2019-. Vanuatu Voices (lexibank/vanuatuvoices CLDF): wordlists 'Nisvai: Blacksands' and 'Nisvai: Ronevie' (369 forms), recorded by A. Shimelman, transcribed by L. Wägerle.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; broad IPA wordlists, 0/369 forms carry a stress mark (U+02C8/U+02CC); no prose.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; practical-orthography lexicon and story texts with no introduction on pronunciation; 0 hits accent/prosod/syllabe/prononc.

sources.citation: Lynch, John & Terry Crowley. 2001. Languages of Vanuatu: A new survey and bibliography. Pacific Linguistics 517. Canberra: ANU. Sec. 3.7.10 'Nisvai' p. 77; p. 71 fn 6.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6211.V36 L96 2001)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6211.V36 L96 2001
sources.note: Nothing for Nisvai: 'The language is known only from Charpentier's (1982b) vocabulary' (p. 77). p. 71 fn 6 (in the Lendamboi section) quotes Charpentier 1982a:63: in 'the languages of the center of the island, there is a strong tonic accent on the next to last syllable, and the final vowel is so destressed as to become almost unrecognizeable' -- a regional remark about interior/centre languages, not attributed to Nisvai.

sources.citation: Lynch, John. 2016. Malakula internal subgrouping: Phonological evidence. Oceanic Linguistics 55(2): 399-431.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Comparative phonology paper using Charpentier's Nisvai data; might relay any Charpentier accent remark or discuss final-vowel reduction linked to penultimate stress in the Southeast Malakula subgroup.

sources.citation: Charpentier, Jean-Michel. 1982. Atlas linguistique du Sud-Malakula / Linguistic atlas of South Malakula (Vanuatu). 2 vols (vol. 1 introduction and phonologies, 177 pp; vol. 2 maps). Paris: SELAF (Langues et cultures du Pacifique 2). ISBN 2-85297-119-4.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only phonological description of Nisvai ('nisvai-vetbong') that exists: vol. 1 gives the phonological systems of the 19 South Malakula languages (Aznar 2019:48; Aznar & Gala 2020 sec. 3) and p. 63 discusses tonic accent for the interior languages (Lynch & Crowley 2001:71 fn 6). Check vol. 1 pp. ~50-70 and the Nisvai phonology for a stress statement, and whether the narrow transcriptions in vol. 2 mark stress.
